idiom_name: class with private/# fields, readonly ids and strict mode
implementation_notes: TypeScript classes are the plainest realization: readonly ids, private members for the compile-time contract, # fields where runtime privacy is required (TypeScript's private is erased), static factories because constructors cannot be private, and explicit command methods. Interfaces describe the seams - repositories, services - rather than the entities, and types disappear at runtime, so invariants still have to be enforced in constructors and factories. Keeping ORM decorators and mapping configuration outside the class preserves persistence ignorance.
pitfalls: private is a compile-time fiction: JavaScript consumers and (order as any) reach the field - use # for state that must not be touched.
Structural typing lets any object with a matching shape substitute for an entity; brand the id types (or add a nominal private field) so Order ids and Customer ids cannot be interchanged.
Decorator-heavy ORMs pull persistence metadata into the model; configure mapping externally so the domain compiles without the framework.
